content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":7,"readability_1x":7,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":6,"appeal":7},"score":61,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The lower-left tentacle mass uses busy alternating blue and cyan stair-steps, becoming noisy at 1x instead of forming clean animated limbs.","The heavy black region between the dome and eyes muddies the face/body connection and makes the construction less readable.","The two eyes are oversized and unevenly integrated; the right eye projects as a box while the left eye is crowded by the central black column.","Several contour transitions are chunky or awkward, especially the upper-right dome, right eye edge, and hooked lower-right tentacle.","Black, white, blue, and cyan occur together in compact areas, making the palette usage harder to reconcile with a single NES sprite palette.","It reads as a cute squid, but mechanical mine cues are weak: there is no obvious casing seam, fuse/light, or distinct warning-eye treatment."],"fixes":["Reduce each eye by roughly one pixel in width and align both pupils and upper edges to create a cleaner Capcom-style face.","Remove one to two black pixels from the central face column so the eyes separate clearly from the body without a large dead black mass.","Simplify the lower-left area into two or three solid tentacle lobes; replace alternating cyan-blue steps with one contiguous shadow cluster and one highlight cluster.","Clean the dome into smoother 1-pixel stair-step runs, especially at the upper-right transition into the face.","Redraw the lower-right hook with a consistent one-pixel outline and a clearer gap between adjacent tentacles.","Reserve white primarily for the eyes and cyan for a single body highlight, keeping each 8x8 region closer to three opaque colors plus transparency.","Add a one- or two-pixel mechanical seam or warning lamp, and provide a separate alert frame that swaps the eye white or pupils to red before detonation."]}
